results.name: heard_all_true_max_point_concentration
results.description: Mean maximum points placed on any single object on trials where the heard word is true of all four objects in the display, testing whether the model under- or over-predicts trial-level betting concentration when semantics rules out no referent.

results.name: heard_duplicate_simple_vs_singleton_complex_diff
results.description: Mean difference in points between the two identical simple true referents (summed) and the singleton complex true referent in heard-word scenes where the word applies to a duplicate pair of fewer-feature objects and a singleton object with more features.
results.code:
# name: heard_duplicate_simple_vs_singleton_complex_diff
# description: Mean difference in points between the two identical simple true referents (summed) and the singleton complex true referent in heard-word scenes where the word applies to a duplicate pair of fewer-feature objects and a singleton object with more features.
def test_statistic(df):
    heard_mask = df["heard"].notna()
    sub = df[heard_mask]
    if len(sub) == 0:
        return 0.0
    scenes = sub[["objects", "heard"]].drop_duplicates()
    scene_info = {}
    for objs_str, h_val in zip(scenes["objects"], scenes["heard"]):
        objs = json.loads(objs_str)
        h = int(h_val)
        true_indices = [i for i, o in enumerate(objs) if o[h] == 1]
        dup_counts = [sum(1 for o2 in objs if o2 == objs[i]) for i in range(len(objs))]
        dup_true = [i for i in true_indices if dup_counts[i] == 2]
        sing_true = [i for i in true_indices if dup_counts[i] == 1]
        if len(dup_true) == 2 and len(sing_true) >= 1:
            f_dup = sum(objs[dup_true[0]])
            complex_sing = [i for i in sing_true if sum(objs[i]) > f_dup]
            if len(complex_sing) >= 1:
                # pick the most feature-rich singleton true referent
                c_idx = max(complex_sing, key=lambda idx: sum(objs[idx]))
                scene_info[(objs_str, h)] = (dup_true[0], dup_true[1], c_idx)
    keys = list(zip(sub["objects"], sub["heard"].astype(int)))
    matched = [scene_info.get(k, None) for k in keys]
    valid_idx = [i for i, m in enumerate(matched) if m is not None]
    if not valid_idx:
        return 0.0
    pts_series = sub["points"].iloc[valid_idx]
    unique_pts = pts_series.unique()
    pts_map = {s: json.loads(s) for s in unique_pts}
    vals = []
    for s, idx in zip(pts_series, valid_idx):
        p = pts_map[s]
        d0, d1, c = matched[idx]
        vals.append((p[d0] + p[d1]) - p[c])
    return float(np.mean(vals))

results.name: heard_false_referent_points_leakage
results.description: Mean total points allocated to semantically false objects (objects lacking the heard feature) on trials where a word was heard and at least one object lacks that feature, testing whether the model's uniform lapse and Dirichlet-multinomial link mispredict points given to false referents.

results.name: heard_max_feature_competitor_points
results.description: Mean points allocated to the most feature-rich true referent in heard-word scenes where multiple objects satisfy the heard word and differ in feature count, testing whether depth-2 RSA over-eliminates complex competitors via scalar implicature.

results.name: prior_two_singletons_with_duplicate_pair_diff
results.description: Mean point difference between the sparser singleton and the richer singleton on prior trials (no word heard) that contain two distinct singletons alongside an identical pair of duplicate objects, testing whether the prior's distinctiveness and feature-count weights distort preference between the two singletons.

results.name: prior_odd_one_out_rich_vs_sparse_asymmetry
results.description: Difference on prior trials between the mean points given to a unique all-features singleton (against featureless duplicates) and the mean points given to a unique featureless singleton (against all-features duplicates), testing feature-count asymmetry when singleton and distinctiveness cues are symmetric.

results.name: heard_equal_complexity_distinct_singleton_points
results.description: Mean points allocated to the most contextually distinctive singleton true referent in heard-word scenes where multiple singletons share the minimum feature count among true referents, probing whether speaker pragmatic choice versus listener prior over- or under-weights singleton distinctiveness.
results.code:
# name: heard_equal_complexity_distinct_singleton_points
# description: Mean points allocated to the most contextually distinctive singleton true referent in heard-word scenes where multiple singletons share the minimum feature count among true referents, probing whether speaker pragmatic choice versus listener prior over- or under-weights singleton distinctiveness.
def test_statistic(df):
    heard_mask = df["heard"].notna()
    sub = df[heard_mask]
    if len(sub) == 0:
        return 0.0
    scenes = sub[["objects", "heard"]].drop_duplicates()
    target_map = {}
    for objs_str, h_val in zip(scenes["objects"], scenes["heard"]):
        objs = json.loads(objs_str)
        h = int(h_val)
        arr = np.array(objs, dtype=float)
        dup_counts = [sum(1 for o2 in objs if o2 == objs[i]) for i in range(len(objs))]
        diff = np.abs(arr[:, None, :] - arr[None, :, :]).sum(axis=(1, 2))
        true_indices = [i for i, o in enumerate(objs) if o[h] == 1]
        if not true_indices:
            continue
        min_f = min(sum(objs[i]) for i in true_indices)
        min_sing_true = [i for i in true_indices if sum(objs[i]) == min_f and dup_counts[i] == 1]
        if len(min_sing_true) >= 2:
            dists = [diff[i] for i in min_sing_true]
            if max(dists) > min(dists):
                best = max(min_sing_true, key=lambda i: diff[i])
                target_map[(objs_str, h)] = best
    keys = list(zip(sub["objects"], sub["heard"].astype(int)))
    t_idx = np.array([target_map.get(k, -1) for k in keys], dtype=np.int64)
    valid = t_idx >= 0
    if not np.any(valid):
        return 0.0
    pts_series = sub["points"].iloc[np.flatnonzero(valid)]
    t_valid = t_idx[valid]
    unique_pts = pts_series.unique()
    pts_map = {s: json.loads(s) for s in unique_pts}
    vals = [pts_map[s][idx] for s, idx in zip(pts_series, t_valid)]
    return float(np.mean(vals))

results.name: prior_all_singleton_featureless_vs_rich_diff
results.description: Mean point difference between the least feature-rich object and the all-features object on prior trials (no word heard) where all four objects are unique singletons, testing whether the model's prior over-favors sparse/distinctive objects over feature-rich objects when singleton status is equal.
